route_1657_status.explanation: Route 1657 is a co-running transit service that shares North GT Road infrastructure between Sarai Peepal Thala (stop 242) and Jahangirpuri GT Road (stop 1245). A single vehicle (DL1PD9231) on October 3 was successfully map-matched to this segment. It is preserved in the training partition (n=84) as a valid North GT Road corridor observation, contributing to physical stop-pair pooling and route baselines, but had no observations in validation or test.

discrepancy_resolution.mathematical_cause: In backend/ml/conformal.py line 39, lower bound is enforced as: lower = np.maximum(y_pred - q, 5.0). When y_pred < q + 5.0 (y_pred < 354.10s), the lower bound is clipped to 5.0s. For 25 of the 30 test predictions, y_pred < 354.10s, truncating the lower interval span from q (349.10s) to (y_pred - 5.0s). The resulting interval width is y_pred + 344.10s, which mathematically reduces the average test interval width from 698.20s to exactly 532.03s.

lower_bound_verification.coverage_impact_analysis: Across all 136 ground-truth segments, the minimum actual segment time is 21.45 seconds. Zero actual segment times are below 5.0 seconds. Because all actual values satisfy y_true >= 21.45s > 5.0s, clipping the lower bound at 5.0s does NOT alter the coverage status of any test observation: unclipped coverage is exactly 26/30 (86.67%), and clipped coverage is exactly 26/30 (86.67%). The 5.0s clipping physically excludes impossible negative travel times without inducing miscoverage.

test_evaluation.coverage_uncertainty_and_clustered_varia: The Clopper-Pearson 95% confidence interval [69.28%, 96.24%] and binomial p-value (p=0.61) are reported strictly as illustrative calculations under an independent Bernoulli trials assumption. In transit reality, clustered observations (intra-vehicle trips and corridor-level spatial correlation) violate independent sampling. Therefore, 90% conformal coverage CANNOT be claimed as statistically demonstrated. Future validation must adopt date/vehicle/stop-pair clustered evaluation strategies.

m0_fallback_tier_reliability.seq9_failure_diagnosis: Segment 1598_dir0_pat0_seq9 had only 2 training observations (count=2 < 3), failing the Tier 1 threshold. Because hourly speed cells for test queries were sparse or absent, M0 fell back to Tier 4 Route Baseline. Tier 4 applied the corridor-wide congested speed (~11 km/h) scaled by detour factor 1.262, predicting 674.87s. In reality, seq9 is a fast free-flow arterial link where buses ran at 24 km/h (239s-252s). This sparse-history fallback caused an error > 420s, pushing the conformal interval lower bound to 325.77s and making all 3 test observations fall below the interval.

vehicles.notes: Vehicle IDs are strictly mutually exclusive across splits (0 overlap). However, within splits, individual vehicles have multiple observations (up to 12), introducing intra-vehicle trip clustering and auto-correlation.

stop_pairs.notes: 12 of 14 test stop pairs overlap with training, reflecting repeated transit link traversals on the corridor. 2 stop pairs in test (Route 1445 seq 2 and 3) are completely unseen in training.

reasons_non_iid: Repeated road link geometry across dates induces spatial autocorrelation.
Same-vehicle sequential runs on a single date introduce driver/vehicle clustering.
Network-level temporal events (Oct 7 outage and evening congestion) induce correlated shock across observations.

random_forest_audit.status_recommendation: Retain Random Forest strictly as an experimental baseline under DEGRADE status, with M0 Historical Median remaining the primary auditable baseline. Although RF achieves 16.11% MAE reduction over M0 on the test partition, the training sample size (n=84) is small, observations are restricted to North GT Road, and trees cannot safely extrapolate to unobserved corridors across Delhi.

mape_vs_medape_audit.explanation: MAPE divides absolute error by actual travel time. In urban bus corridors, short stop-to-stop links (20s-60s) yield 200%-435% relative error when models predict conservative corridor speeds. Because MAPE is asymmetric and heavily penalizes over-predictions on small denominators, a small number of high-percentage outliers inflates the arithmetic mean above 100%. MedAPE is robust to this skew: M2 MedAPE is 51.64% vs M0 MedAPE of 92.99%, demonstrating substantial predictive gain.

scope_and_provenance_levels.LEVEL_1_DIRECT_OBSERVATION: 136 GPS-verified stop-to-stop segment observations derived from 199 stop crossings on 26 distinct stop pairs across 5 dates (Oct 1-4, 7). Highest fidelity, narrow spatial scope.
scope_and_provenance_levels.LEVEL_2_HISTORICAL_STATISTICAL_BASELINE: Hierarchical Historical Median (M0) with Tiers 1-4 fallback. Deterministic, transparent, distribution-free quantiles. Primary auditable baseline.
scope_and_provenance_levels.LEVEL_3_EXPERIMENTAL_ML: Ridge (M1) and Random Forest (M2) trained on log travel time. Evaluated on Oct 7; retained as experimental benchmark under DEGRADE.
scope_and_provenance_levels.LEVEL_4_TIMETABLE_FALLBACK: Static GTFS scheduled times and corridor default velocity (18 km/h). Used when no GPS ground truth exists.
scope_and_provenance_levels.detour_factor_scope: Calibrated detour factor k=1.262 is local to North GT Road (ISBT Kashmiri Gate to Jahangirpuri) and must NOT be applied network-wide.
